panels.title: Build
panels.description: Version, commit and Go version of each running replica.

panels.title: Submissions/sec
panels.description: Submission attempts per second, across all outcomes.

panels.title: Success ratio
panels.description: Share of submissions that were delivered successfully. Honeypot and AI spam drops are not counted as success, even though the client receives HTTP 200.

panels.title: Delivery failure ratio
panels.description: Share of channel delivery attempts that failed. status=failure covers both a template render failure and a send failure.

panels.title: HTTP in flight
panels.description: Requests currently being handled on the public submission listener.

panels.title: Background dispatches
panels.description: Async submissions whose spam-filter and delivery work is still running. Only forms with response_mode: async populate this. A sustained climb means dispatches are piling up faster than they drain.

panels.title: Submissions by outcome
panels.description: The full status vocabulary, same as the audit log's status field: success, validation_failed, origin_denied, auth_denied, rate_limited, spam_dropped_honeypot, captcha_failed, spam_dropped_ai, delivery_failed.

panels.title: Submissions by form
panels.description: Per-form submission rate, across all outcomes.

panels.title: Outcome breakdown (selected range)
panels.description: Total submissions per outcome over the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: Deliveries by status
panels.description: Channel delivery attempts. status=rate_limited means this channel's own outbound rate_limit rejected it or it timed out waiting for capacity.

panels.title: Failures by channel
panels.description: status=failure covers both a template render failure and a send failure.

panels.title: Delivery latency
panels.description:
Time spent delivering to a channel, including template rendering.

Buckets top out at 10s and the per-send timeout is also 10s, so a p99 pinned at the top bucket means sends are timing out, not merely slow.

panels.title: Delivery latency distribution
panels.description: Bucket boundaries are .05 .1 .25 .5 1 2.5 5 10 seconds. The top row is everything above 10s.

panels.title: Deliveries per channel (selected range)
panels.description: channel is the form's own channels[].id

panels.title: Honeypot drops
panels.description: Submissions dropped by the honeypot field check. The client still receives HTTP 200.

panels.title: CAPTCHA verifications
panels.description:
provider is the form's captcha.provider (turnstile, hcaptcha, recaptcha_v2, recaptcha_v3, generic).

status=failed means the token was rejected. status=error means the verify call itself errored, typically a provider outage, resolved by captcha.on_error.

panels.title: AI spam verdicts
panels.description: AI classifier verdicts. verdict=error also covers calls that never reached the provider because the spam filter's outbound rate limit was exceeded.

panels.title: Spam filter actions
panels.description: The resolved on_spam / on_error outcome. trigger is spam or error; action is deliver, deliver_tagged, drop or route.

panels.title: AI classifier latency
panels.description:
Time spent in the AI classifier call.

This histogram uses the Prometheus default buckets, topping out at 10s, so p90/p99 saturate for slow calls. The mean is the more reliable figure.

panels.title: Inbound rejections by scope
panels.description: Requests rejected by the inbound rate limiter. scope is global, per_ip or per_form, checked in that order.

panels.title: Active rate-limit buckets
panels.description:
Memory backend only. With rate_limit.backend: valkey the bucket state lives in Valkey and this metric has no series.

scope is global, ip or form. Sampled every 15s.

panels.title: Rate-limit backend errors
panels.description:
Valkey backend only.

Connectivity or timeout errors talking to the backend, not a normal deny. rate_limit.on_error decides whether the request still goes through.

panels.title: Outbound rate-limit wait (p95)
panels.description:
Time spent waiting for an outbound token. target is either a channel id or the literal spam_filter.

Only recorded when waiting actually happened (on_limit: wait).

panels.title: Since last successful reload
panels.description: Time since the config currently in use was loaded. Failed reloads do not update this.

panels.title: Config reload attempts
panels.description: Reload attempts from startup, the file watcher, SIGHUP, or the internal /reload endpoint.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: go_memstats_alloc_bytes is Go heap currently allocated; process_resident_memory_bytes is RSS as seen by the OS.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores used.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Approaching process_max_fds will start failing outbound SMTP/HTTP sends.

list.description: formelay_build_info has exactly one series per replica, which makes it the cleanest source for the instance list.
